pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis secondary to an Ovarian Teratoma THE SMOKING GUN: The continuous EEG showing an "extreme delta brush" pattern, which prompted a targeted pelvic ultrasound revealing an occult, mature cystic teratoma of the right ovary. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Ectopic neural tissue residing within the ovarian teratoma expresses the GluN1 subunit of the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor. The host immune system mounts an antibody response against these antigens, generating pathogenic IgG autoantibodies that cross the blood-brain barrier. These antibodies selectively bind to, cross-link, and internalize NMDA receptors on inhibitory GABAergic cortical and subcortical interneurons. The resulting loss of central inhibition leads to excessive extracellular glutamate, frontal-striatal disinhibition, profound psychiatric disturbances, extrapyramidal movement disorders, hypoventilation, and severe dysregulation of the autonomic nervous system.
